key_features.classic_presentation: Ectopic pregnancy presents with lower abdominal/pelvic pain and vaginal bleeding in a woman of reproductive age with missed period. Pain may be unilateral. Can rupture causing life-threatening hemorrhage. Any woman of childbearing age with abdominal pain needs pregnancy test.
key_features.typical_demographics: Women of reproductive age (15-45). Risk factors: prior ectopic, PID, tubal surgery, IUD.
key_features.pathophysiology_brief: Embryo implants outside uterus (usually fallopian tube). As it grows, can rupture causing hemorrhage.

diagnostic_questions.context: ALWAYS consider in women of reproductive age. Pregnancy test mandatory.
Missed period is key finding. May be subtle (1-2 weeks late).
Abnormal vaginal bleeding in 75%. Usually light, not like normal period.
Often unilateral (side of ectopic) but can be diffuse.
Shoulder pain indicates intraperitoneal bleeding (blood irritating diaphragm).

red_flags.action: Ruptured ectopic with hemorrhagic shock - life-threatening emergency

red_flags.finding: Severe sudden-onset pain with missed period

typical_management: Immediate OB/GYN consultation. Transvaginal ultrasound, quantitative hCG. Treatment: methotrexate if unruptured, surgery if ruptured.
disposition: Emergency department for any suspected ectopic. Potentially life-threatening.
patient_education: Ectopic pregnancy is a pregnancy outside the uterus. It cannot develop normally and can be life-threatening if it ruptures. Requires immediate medical care.
